118990.note: Moved the pin 190 m south, from open sagebrush onto the station's large tan roof (about 13 by 9 m), the building the Forest Service's point touches; a smaller building stands 8 m north of it. The drawn road passes about 40 m north, past an undrawn parking area.

231968.note: The pin sits on open ground among junipers inside a bend of the drawn road, 11 m from it, with no pad or clearing that marks the group camp; the listing's own point is 86 km away (a bad listing point).

232030.note: The pin is on the open camp area 15 m south of the group campground's building, beside the drawn loop; nothing drawn reaches the pin itself. The listing's own point is 5.6 km away.

232057.note: The pin is beside the drawn road through the equestrian camp, in the open between its lanes; nothing at the pin itself marks the group site among the camp's spurs.

232348.note: The Forest Service's point names the Loon Lake equestrian group camp, a different place from the chalet, so it can't place this unit; it sits on a camp lane among trailers 145 m southeast. The pin is in the trees inside the paved parking loop with no building that could be the chalet. Not moved.

232790.note: The pin sits on an open hillside above a housing tract, 130 m from any drawn road, with nothing at it that could be a campground; the listing's own point is 640 m away.

233126.note: The pin sits in forest on a slope 130 m from the nearest drawn road, with no building, tower or clearing at it.

233183.note: The pin is on open grass at the edge of an oak wood 37 m from the drawn road; no group site clearing, table or shelter shows within 200 m, and the campground's loops lie farther southeast.

233357.note: The pin sits in open pines 20 m west of a few small structures and vehicles, 35 m south of the drawn loop; no corral is plain at the pin, and nothing drawn reaches it.

233381.note: The pin is on the bare clearing of the group camp at the end of the drawn spur below the ranch buildings.

233398.note: The pin is on the drawn spur north of the meadow road under canopy, where only the spur's line shows; nothing at the pin marks the group site, but the spur reaches it.

233982.note: The pin is in the meadow 20 m southeast of the guard station's red-roofed building at the forest edge; the drawn spur ends 40 m west of the building, and the short way to it doesn't show plainly enough to trace.

233988.note: The pin is in unbroken forest and the Forest Service's point 68 m north is on the river's open gravel bar; neither shows a group site's pad, tables or road. Not moved.

234144.note: Moved the pin 78 m east, from the empty turnaround onto the larger of two dark roofs at the end of the drawn spur, the guard station; the spur ends 14 m from it. The Forest Service's point is 40 m further east, in the trees, so it was not used as the spot.

234157.note: The gray-roofed cabin shows plainly 85 m southwest of the pin at the meadow's edge, with a path to it; the pin was in unbroken forest and now sits on the cabin.

234160.note: The pin sits in a burned stand of standing dead trees 315 m from the nearest drawn road, with no cabin or clearing at it.

234161.note: The pin sits on a brushy slope 300 m below the drawn road, with no tower or building at it; the lookout is likely on the summit by the road's end.

234170.note: The pin is on the cabin in its clearing on the butte, where the drawn spur off the loop ends.

234224.note: The dense lidar (14.73 ground points per square meter) shows a building footprint on a levelled pad by the pin, and the photo shows its blue-gray roof under the oaks. Re-centered Old Stage Drive past it onto the pavement, which OpenStreetMap drew 6 to 12 m east of the road for about 200 m; it now follows the road within about 3 m, 34 m west of the pin. But the listing's own point, 490 m north-east, sits on a cluster of small buildings at the end of a drawn road, so which is the guard station cabin can't be told; nothing was moved.

234281.note: The pin is beside the lookout on the bare summit, and the drawn trail from the road reaches it.

234292.note: The pin is on the lookout on the bare ridge, where the drawn trails meet; the drawn road stops 30 m short, on the ridge's west side.

234321.note: The lidar relief shows the drawn track down the meadow as a pair of wheel ruts, with the drawn line beside them, ending near the pin, but neither layer shows a roof, levelled pad or clearing edge at the pin (the meadow is open grass there), and the photo shows only the forest's shadow. Nothing traced.

234326.note: The dense lidar (8.48 ground points per square meter) shows the pin in a meadow at the end of the drawn track, with only a small raised patch about 3 by 5 m 4 m west of it in the relief and nothing plainly a cabin footprint or levelled pad; the photo shows snow with a small dark shape 5 m north that may be a roof or a shadow. The cabin can't be confirmed, so nothing was traced or moved.

234395.note: The pin is beside the lookout building on the bare summit, inside the drawn loop at the road's end.

234408.note: The pin is on the cabin on the butte top, where the drawn road ends in its bare turnaround.

234435.note: The pin is on the bare clearing beside a small building on the ridge, 40 m from the drawn road; the dirt loop from the road round the clearing to the building shows but isn't drawn, and the drawn road runs about 10 m west of the visible one. The listing's own point is 580 m away.

234444.note: The pin is on the cabin's roof in its small clearing, and the drawn trail passes beside it (it is reached by trail; no road is near).

234482.note: The Forest Service's point ("Cold Springs Peak Lookout"), 110 m north of the pin up the open crest, shows bare ground, two small trees and pale rock in the photo, and the dense ground relief shows no building gap or levelled pad there; the pin on the scarp top shows none either. Not moved.

234601.note: The pin is on a building among the structures and parked vehicles in the clearing, inside the drawn loop at the road's end; the drawn loop runs a little off the visible lane around the rocks.

234631.note: The pin sits in the station's pasture 12 m north of its gravel drive, which wasn't drawn and was traced from the road to the yard; the guard station's buildings are 85 m southwest of the pin, so the pin is near but not on the station.

252037.note: The pin is on the lookout on the bare summit, where the drawn road ends in its loop.

262759.note: The pin is on the small shelter in a clearing in the logged stand, at the end of a plain dirt lane 150 m long that isn't drawn; the lane fades into the trees 25 m short of the drawn road, so it wasn't traced. The drawn road west of it runs a few metres off the visible gravel road.

10038994.note: The lidar relief shows the road to the southwest as a plain graded band with the drawn road on it, but neither layer shows the drawn loop or a pad or clearing at the pin inside it (the intensity is only a smoother gray patch among the tree crowns, and the relief even forest floor); the listing's own point is about 1,690 km away. Nothing traced.

10116515.note: The pin is on the guard station's roof in its bare yard, where the drawn road ends.

10116518.note: Zoomed in, a brown-roofed cabin about 7 m across stands right at the pin, with a dirt lane running to it from the drawn road 45 m north; the pin is already on it.

10165105.note: Unchanged. The pin is in unbroken forest between the switchbacks of the McKenzie Highway, about 120 m north of the road; the only spur near it (Forest Road 4200-246, about 290 m west) is a short stub under full canopy, and no campground, loop or clearing shows, so nothing was moved.

10165155.note: The pin, at the listing's own point, is in unbroken forest by the drawn road; the dirt loop 140 m northwest has clearings and a parked vehicle but nothing that marks which part, if any, is the group site.

10165165.note: The outline holds a road end with a turnaround and small buildings in the trees on the lake shore, which reads as the campground. The point is on the approach road about 120 m west of it, not at its entrance.

10165200.note: Unchanged after the rebuild: no outline. The pin is in an open meadow between the highway and a side road with no pads or loops near it; the only campground-like spot, a small loop with a restroom 600 m south, may be another site and isn't plainly Caribou, so the pin wasn't moved.

10165205.note: The outline follows the strip campground along the river, with its spur road, pads and turnaround at the south end. The point is about 60 m north of it, at a cluster of buildings on the road in, not inside the campground.

10165220.note: The outline holds a lakeshore loop with pads and campers on the photo, and the point is inside it.

10165285.note: There's no outline. The pin is among small road loops with trailers and tents beside the lake, with a resort's buildings and marina just north, so a campground is plainly within about 100 m.

10165305.note: Unchanged. The pin is in unbroken forest about 250 m northwest of Waldo Road, and neither Gold Lake nor any campground, loop or clearing shows anywhere in the 1.4 km frame, so there's nothing to move it to.

10165320.note: There's no outline. The lidar intensity shows the campground's gravel roads as bright bands under the trees, with the drawn roads on them, and the pin sits 60 m east of the loop road where the photo shows parked vehicles and pull-ins; the restroom is about 90 m away, so it reads as the campground. Nothing traced.

10165360.note: Unchanged. The pin is already on the gravel lane that runs beside the Salmon River Scenic Byway to a small turnaround loop with one small building; that may be the campground, but no pads, tables or campers show along it, so the photo doesn't plainly show one and there was nothing to move it to.

10165375.note: Unchanged. The pin is in unbroken forest north of Forest Road 21; an OpenStreetMap spur with a toilet tag about 210 m west-southwest may be the campground, but it lies under full canopy and the photo shows neither the spur nor any pad, so nothing was moved.

10165385.note: The outline wraps a spur road with small clearings along it, which looks like a campground spur. The point is about 80 m east of it on the road in, past the outline's end.

10165430.note: Unchanged after the rebuild: no outline. The pin is in dense forest beside the river road; two small road loops on the river bench lie 80 m and 400 m north-west, and with an Upper O'Brien campground on the same stretch the photo can't say which loop is Lower O'Brien, so the pin wasn't moved.

10165470.note: The outline follows the campground's loops and pads between the highway and the river, and the point is inside it on the campground road.

10165485.note: The lidar intensity shows the campground loop and its pull-in pads plainly under the trees, with the drawn loop on them; OpenStreetMap's outline holds it plus a good deal of extra forest and the lakeside road to the west, and the point sits on the outline's northeast edge, near the road in. Nothing traced.

10165490.note: The outline follows a lakeshore loop with pads, separate from the larger campground to the north, and the point is inside it.

10165495.note: Moved the pin about 220 m north-northwest from an open meadow into the camping loop off North Fork Canyon Road, where trailers sit on pads around the lane; it's the only campground loop within a kilometer (Caribou and North Fork are 1.7 to 1.9 km off). There's no outline, so the map shows the pin there.

10165510.note: The outline follows the campground's dirt loops and pads between the road and the lakeshore, and the point is inside it at the east end.

10165530.note: The outline holds the loop by the lake with pads, and the point is inside it. A second loop with campers just west is left outside the outline.

10165581.note: The outline holds the campground's spurs and pads on both sides of the highway, and the highway itself runs through it. The point is on the highway at the outline's northeast edge.

10165591.note: The outline holds a spur road with a loop at each end under heavy forest by the creek, and the point is inside it. The trees hide the pads, so the fit can't be checked closely.

10165596.note: The outline holds the campground's loops and pads on both sides of the highway. The point sits about 15 m outside it, in the river.

10165606.note: Unchanged. The pin is in the shallow south arm of Scott Lake; Forest Road 4200-260 runs past under full canopy to a trailhead lot about 450 m west, and the only sign of camping is a couple of cars along the road south of the lake, so no campground plainly shows to move it to.

10165626.note: The lidar relief (2.21 ground points per square meter) shows a graded lane, a smooth band with levelled benches beside it, running about 200 m along the terrace between the road and the creek from the bridge, and OpenStreetMap's narrow outline holds it with the drawn inner lane along it; the point sits inside the outline on its creek-side edge. Pads can't be told apart under the trees, and the listing says the campground is closed. Nothing traced.

10165631.note: Unchanged. The pin is already on the gravel lot at the end of road 1957, the likely parking for the campground, but everything around it is under full canopy and no pads, tents or loop show, so the photo doesn't plainly show a campground and there was nothing to move it to.

10165636.note: The outline follows the campground's loops and pads above the lakeshore. The point is on its northeast edge at a large paved lot by the water, not at the campground's road in.

10165656.note: The outline holds a lakeshore strip with pads and campers under the trees, and the point is about 20 m outside its south end in the forest. A separate loop to the east is a different outline.

10165721.note: Unchanged. The pin is on a gravel bar at the river's edge; a small loop with bare pull-outs about 90 m northwest may be Upper O'Brien, but no campers show and Lower O'Brien's loop is 400 m east on the same road, so it isn't plainly the one named and nothing was moved.

10165741.note: The outline follows the small loop by the river, and the point is inside it next to a restroom building.

10191065.note: Moved the pin about 245 m west from the meadow east of Rock Creek Road into the wide gravel camping loop west of the road, beside its toilet, with trailers parked around its edge (RIDB's own Diamondfield Jack entry also sits by it). There's no outline, so the map shows the pin there.

10191075.note: Unchanged after the rebuild: the map takes the outline OpenStreetMap names Lake Cleveland Campground on the north shore, 85 m east of the point, which holds two loops (west and east) with pads. A second, unnamed outline with a lane and restroom sits at the lake's south-west end. For a listing named West Side, the photo can't say whether that is the north campground's west loop or the south-west camp, so nothing was moved.

10191090.note: Moved the pin about 135 m northwest from the meadow east of Rock Creek Road onto the lane OpenStreetMap names Pettit Campground, west of the road, whose spurs, pads and Spur A loop show among the trees; Diamondfield Jack is 1.3 km off. There's no outline, so the map shows the pin there.

10191095.note: There's no outline. The photo and both lidar layers show the campground's gravel loop and lanes off the highway by the creek, with the drawn lanes on them within a few meters, and the pin sits in the bare ground between the loop and the highway, within 30 m of them, so it reads as the campground. Nothing traced.

10191100.note: Unchanged. The pin is on a bare hillside east of Rock Creek Road; about 100 m southwest a gravel pull-out with a short lane into a grove by the creek may be the campground, but no pads, tables or campers show there, so the photo doesn't plainly show one and nothing was moved.

10191105.note: The outline follows the campground's ring road around a grove, with campers parked inside, and the point is inside it.

10191110.note: The outline follows a loop road with spur pads under the trees, and the point is inside it.

10192037.note: There's no outline. The lidar relief shows the campground's lanes and spur loops as crowned bands under the pines, with the drawn roads on or within about 5 m of them, and the pin sits in a hollow beside the small east loop, inside the road network, so it reads as the campground; the intensity is too mottled to add anything, and the loop around the pin can't be checked closely enough to redraw. Nothing traced.

10192067.note: Unchanged. The pin is at the end of a short track in open scrub; a dirt loop about 150 m west (where RIDB's other Horse Springs entry sits) may be the campground, but no pads, tables or campers show along it, so the photo doesn't plainly show one and nothing was moved.

10192122.note: The outline follows the campground's loop road and its entrance spur from the highway, and the point is inside the loop.

10215854.note: There's no outline. The photo shows the campground's dirt pull-ins and a small building in the open strip along the creek, and the pin sits at its east edge beside the paved road, which the lidar intensity shows as a dark band with the drawn road within a few meters of it; it reads as the campground. Nothing traced.

10215884.note: There's no outline. The pin is beside a cluster of spur roads with pull-ins and small shade structures by the river, which reads as the campground.

10215904.note: Unchanged after the rebuild: no outline. The pin is in mesquite scrub between the highway and a dirt road along the river; no pads, loop or campers show anywhere near it in the frame, so there is nothing to move it onto.

10215919.note: Unchanged after the rebuild: no outline. The pin is in scrub on the dirt loop above the river; one small structure and a cleared lot 250 m west by the road aren't enough to show a campground, and no pads or campers show near the pin, so it wasn't moved.

10221637.note: Rebuilt with the outline-name check: the map no longer takes South Fork's outline and shows the pin 'About here' instead. But the pin is in the creekside trees just north of South Fork Campground, and nothing across the creek or nearby plainly shows a separate Davis Flat camp (the open flat to the east has only scattered oaks and tracks), so the pin would still send a camper to South Fork's loops; nothing was moved.

10221647.note: The outline follows a creekside strip with loops and pads, which OpenStreetMap names Fouts Campground. The point is about 60 m east of it, across the creek in scrub by the road.

10221657.note: The outline holds a small loop with pads and a structure beside the road. The point is about 40 m east of it, across the creek.

10221662.note: The outline holds a small loop with pads off the road, and the point is about 20 m east of it by the road junction that leads in.

10221667.note: The outline holds a clearing with a loop road, pads and a few vehicles in burned forest. The point is about 30 m east of it in the trees.

10221672.note: The outline holds a small loop with pads beside the river, and the point is inside it.

10221677.note: The outline follows the creekside loops with pads that OpenStreetMap names South Fork Campground. The point is about 25 m east of it, across the creek.

10293118.note: The pin is on the ranger office building beside the drawn road, which passes 10 m east.

10314707.note: Unchanged. The pin is in dense forest by the Little Naches River; the only campground in the frame is a small loop with a toilet about 450 m west-southwest that OpenStreetMap names Longmire Meadow, reached by road 1906 where the listing's directions say road 1902, so it isn't plainly the one named and nothing was moved.

10327336.note: The pin is on the small shelter at the east edge of the big bare clearing of the equestrian area; the drawn spur stops at the clearing's north edge, 55 m from the shelter.

10386715.note: The pin is in the open stock yard east of the station's buildings, 20 m from the drawn road that passes it.
